sections.content: You know *en resumen* from B1 Unit 13 and *en conclusión* from B1 Unit 17. Two more closing phrases are *en definitiva* ("all in all", "in the end") and *en suma* ("in short"). They all come at the end of a text and bring together what you said before. *En resumen* repeats the main points briefly. *En conclusión* gives what you conclude. *En definitiva* gives the final judgement after weighing the points. *En suma* gathers everything into one short sentence.

sections.title: Four ways to close
rows: En resumen, el curso es útil pero caro.
To sum up, the course is useful but expensive.
In conclusion, I recommend the course.
En definitiva, vale la pena, aunque cuesta mucho.
All in all, it is worth it, although it costs a lot.
En suma, un buen curso a un precio alto.
In short, a good course at a high price.

sections.content: A closing marker needs earlier points to close, so it never opens a text. It takes a comma, and one closing marker at the end is enough.
